summary.headline: Orders and revenue beat their weekly targets, but QTD and YTD revenue remain behind target, and the 14-Day Return Rate rose notably.

points.what: Orders were 938 for the week, 102.5% of the 915 target, even though they fell 3.2% from the prior week's 969.
points.so_what: The week cleared its target despite the week-over-week pullback, showing target attainment and week-over-week direction do not always move together.

points.what: Revenue was $67,708, 106.5% of the $63,587 target, though down 5.4% from the prior week.
points.so_what: Revenue outperformed its weekly target even while declining from the previous week.

points.what: QTD revenue is at 99.3% of target and YTD revenue is at 95.7% of target.
points.so_what: Despite this week's target beat, the quarter and the year remain behind target.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 11 May rose to 10.9%, a change marked as notable.
points.so_what: This flags a risk in order quality moving in the wrong direction.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 11 May rose to 10.9%, up 1.0 pp WoW and up 2.0 pp YoY, both marked bad and notable.
points.so_what: Returns are rising against both last week and last year, a risk to watch on order quality.

points.what: QTD revenue is at 99.3% of target, a gap of $4,397, with $288,597 still needed over the remaining 4 weeks to reach the $884,086 full-quarter target.
points.so_what: The quarter remains behind target and this week's beat alone did not close the gap.

points.what: The required weekly revenue run-rate for the rest of the year is $83,008, above the current 8-week run-rate of $66,763.
points.so_what: At the current pace, revenue is running below what is needed to reach the full-year target.

points.what: Orders were 102.5% of target and revenue was 106.5% of target this week.
points.so_what: The week was ahead of target on both orders and revenue.

points.what: QTD revenue is 99.3% of target, with $288,597 still needed across the remaining 4 weeks to hit the $884,086 full-quarter target.
points.so_what: The quarter needs stronger weeks ahead, since one week ahead of target did not close the quarterly gap.

points.what: YTD revenue is 95.7% of target, and the required weekly run-rate for the rest of the year is $83,008 versus a current 8-week run-rate of $66,763.
points.so_what: The current pace is below what full-year attainment requires.

points.what: APAC orders fell 9.5% WoW and contributed -41 to the week's order change, 132.3% of the total change.
points.so_what: APAC was the largest single drag on this week's order decline.

points.what: EMEA orders rose 24.4% WoW and contributed +42 to the change, the only region with a positive contribution.
points.so_what: EMEA growth partly offset the declines in APAC, North America, and LATAM.

points.what: Search orders fell 2.0% WoW and contributed -13, the largest share of change among traffic sources at 41.9%.
points.so_what: Search was the biggest driver of the traffic-source decline in orders this week.

points.what: AOV was $84.53, down 3.7% from the prior week's $87.74, though up 6.6% YoY.
points.so_what: This week's revenue is not coming from bigger baskets, since AOV fell versus last week.

points.what: The cancellation rate fell 1.2 pp to 14.6%, a notable improvement, and also down YoY.
points.so_what: A lower cancellation rate means more of this week's orders counted toward revenue.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 11 May rose to 10.9%, up 1.0 pp WoW and up 2.0 pp YoY.
points.so_what: Rising returns against both comparisons is a risk to order quality to keep watching.

points.what: New signups rose 16.0% WoW to 261, a notable increase, and were up 8.3% YoY versus 67.5% YoY growth in orders.
points.so_what: Order growth YoY is far outpacing new signup growth YoY.

checks.name: 14-Day Return Rate names its mature week
anomaly flag acknowledged in the summary
sentences at most 30 words and 4 numbers
each slot only covers its allowed KPIs

no causes, recommendations, 'plan', or ': watchouts point 1 so_what: calls revenue net ('net revenue')

points.what: APAC orders fell to 392, down 9.5% WoW, accounting for 132.3% of the week's total order change.
points.so_what: This makes APAC the largest driver of this week's order decline, worth tracking against next week's target.

points.what: EMEA orders rose to 214, up 24.4% WoW, contributing +42 orders toward the week's total change.
points.so_what: EMEA's growth partly offset declines elsewhere, but not enough to prevent the overall WoW drop in orders.

points.what: Search orders fell to 650, down 2.0% WoW, but still accounted for 41.9% of the week's total order change.
points.so_what: Search is by far the largest traffic source, so even a small decline there weighs heavily on total orders.

points.what: AOV fell to $84.53, down 3.7% WoW (bad), though still up 6.6% YoY.
points.so_what: Revenue growth this week came from order volume more than from bigger baskets: per-order value fell WoW.

points.what: Cancellation rate fell to 14.6%, down 1.2pp WoW (a notable, good change) and down 2.5pp YoY.
points.so_what: Each point of cancellation is worth about $793 in revenue, so this improvement helped support this week's revenue.

points.what: New signups rose to 261, up 16.0% WoW (notable, good) and up 8.3% YoY.
points.so_what: Signups grew faster than orders this week: orders fell 3.2% WoW while signups rose, showing the two moved in opposite directions.

summary.headline: Orders and revenue were ahead of weekly target, but the quarter (99.3%) and year (95.7%) remain behind target on revenue.

points.what: Orders were 938 for the week, 102.5% of target, though down 3.2% from the prior week (a bad WoW result).
points.so_what: The weekly target was met, but the softer WoW trend comes as QTD revenue remains behind target.

points.what: Revenue was $67,708, 106.5% of target, but down 5.4% WoW (bad).
points.so_what: This week's revenue beat target, but the WoW decline combined with a falling AOV means the gain reflects volume more than bigger baskets.

points.what: QTD revenue attainment is 99.3% of target and YTD attainment is 95.7%, both behind target.
points.so_what: Despite this week's win, the quarter and year remain behind, keeping full-year risk elevated.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 11 May rose to 10.9%, up 1.0pp WoW, a notable increase.
points.so_what: This marks a reversal after several weeks of falling returns, a risk worth watching alongside the quarter's shortfall.

points.what: Weekly orders were 102.5% of target and weekly revenue was 106.5% of target, both ahead this week.
points.so_what: Next week's targets rise to 1,006 orders and $74,990 in revenue, higher bars than this week already met.

points.what: The quarter needs $288,597 more to reach the full quarter target of $884,086, with 4 weeks left.
points.so_what: This keeps the quarter at risk without stronger weeks ahead than the one just closed.

points.what: YTD revenue attainment is 95.7% of target, and the required weekly run-rate for the rest of the year is $83,008 versus a recent 8-week run-rate of $66,763.
points.so_what: The recent pace is below what's needed for the rest of the year, keeping the full-year target at risk.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate (week of 11 May) rose to 10.9%, up 1.0pp WoW and up 2.0pp YoY (both bad).
points.so_what: Two consecutive bad reads mean the improvement seen earlier in the year is not holding, adding risk to net revenue if the trend continues.

points.what: QTD revenue attainment is 99.3% of target, a gap of -$4,397, with 4 weeks left in the quarter.
points.so_what: Closing this gap requires stronger weeks over the remaining quarter, or the quarter will miss its target.

points.what: AOV fell to $84.53, down 3.7% WoW (bad), though still up 6.6% YoY.
points.so_what: This week's revenue results relied on order volume more than basket size, and order volume itself was down WoW too.
